A1.justification: The PDFs describe the same study, with matching methods, equations and main figures. However, v1 references Supplementary Text 1, Table 1 and Figure 1 that are absent from the supplied PDF. Their relationship to v2's included appendices cannot be fully established.

before.justification: v1 reports original capacity-curve fitting, model training and held-out cycle-life predictions, including results in Figures 3, 6 and 7.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results and includes further feature correlations and individual prediction plots in Appendices A–C.

M1.justification: Both versions use the same capacity-loss equation, five selected features, self-attention regression and two-stage training objectives. Replacing Q(0) with the explicitly defined C and renaming other variables clarify notation without changing the procedure.

E1.justification: Both evaluate the same Severson battery dataset using early-cycle information and the same primary and secondary test coverage. v2 discusses an 85% capacity threshold but does not report evaluation under that threshold or on another dataset.

E2.justification: The ElasticNet baseline and comparisons with Severson et al.'s reported full-model results remain. v2 clarifies that ElasticNet uses the selected features to predict A and B; the unchanged comparison and scores support treating this as additional documentation rather than an established baseline revision.

E3.justification: The reported splits, preprocessing, metrics, end-of-life threshold and ElasticNet tuning ranges remain unchanged. v2's epoch counts and learning rates specify previously unstated settings, without establishing a changed training budget or evaluation protocol.

E4.justification: The supplied v2 expands the documented feature-selection and training-stage diagnostics through Table 1 and Figures 8–9, including Stage 1 prediction scatter and many individual capacity curves. v1 already compares training stages through aggregate RMSE in Figure 6. These are limited extensions of existing analyses; the contents of v1's unavailable supplement remain unknown.

E5.justification: Neither PDF reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals or significance tests. Additional feature correlations and battery-level prediction plots do not introduce a new uncertainty-reporting practice.

E6.justification: Main results remain unchanged, including primary and secondary test RMSEs of 127.83 and 179.92 cycles. v2 additionally presents candidate-feature correlations, such as DeltaQ_logSkew correlations of 0.28 and -0.18, and individual predictions after each training stage. Figure 8(b) repeats the existing final-stage scatter rather than showing improved performance.

T1.justification: A new footnote in Section 3.1 explicitly assumes equal cycle durations to justify replacing time dependence with cycle-number dependence. This adds a modeling assumption supporting the equation; the remaining mathematical changes are equivalent notation, with no new theorem or proof.

C1.justification: The abstract and conclusion retain the same central contributions: reconstructing complete capacity-loss curves through a physics-informed attention model, achieving comparable cycle-life accuracy, and supporting different end-of-life thresholds without retraining. The expanded introduction explains rather than broadens these claims.

C2.justification: v2 attributes initial capacity loss to calendar aging and formation cycles and explains the use of nominal capacity as a common reference. Section 4 also newly attributes ElasticNet's poor performance to its limited ability to capture nonlinear degradation patterns.

D1.justification: v2 specifies 800 epochs at learning rate 10^-3 followed by 3000 epochs at 5×10^-5, and clarifies feature construction and baseline inputs and outputs. Code remains available upon request. Some new Table 1 descriptions are inconsistent with Section 3.3, notably variance of logarithmic changes versus logarithm of variance.

R1.justification: v2 adds Schauser et al. (2022) and Sours et al. (2024) to support discussion of alternative end-of-life thresholds. The existing literature and positioning of the hybrid method remain substantially unchanged; expanded bibliographic names are formatting changes.

P1.justification: v2 makes localized explanatory rewrites, expands feature definitions, corrects wording and adds Appendices A–C while preserving the main section sequence. It also removes keywords, acknowledgements and the patent disclosure.

P2.justification: The document is globally reformatted with smaller type, wider text blocks and rescaled, reflowed figures. The seven main figure images remain identical, but Table 1 and Figures 8–9 add a substantial supplementary display, including dense capacity-curve grids and a training-stage comparison that partly redisplays Figure 7(a).

improvement.justification: Clarifying the ElasticNet baseline and documenting training schedules makes the existing comparison easier to interpret and reproduce. The appendices also expose more evidence behind feature selection and two-stage training. These are limited net gains: feature-description inconsistencies and crowded appendix plots reduce their usefulness, while removal of the patent disclosure weakens transparency. The main scientific findings remain unchanged.
